headline: 2 dead, 4 injured as roof collapses at under-construction building in Pirganj
summary: The accident occurred at a municipal building under construction in Pirganj, Rangpur, leaving two workers dead and several others injured.
details: Two workers were killed and four others were injured after the roof of an under-construction municipal building collapsed in Pirganj, Rangpur.
The incident occurred while construction work was ongoing at the site, causing the structure to give way and trap several workers underneath.
Rescue operations were launched immediately to recover the victims from the debris, with local authorities and emergency services arriving at the scene.
The four injured workers were rushed to the nearest hospital for medical treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were recovered from the rubble.
Local residents and officials gathered at the site as heavy machinery was used to clear the collapsed roof and search for any other trapped individuals.
caption:
A tragic construction accident in Rangpur has left two workers dead and four others injured.

Two workers were killed and four others were injured after the roof of an under-construction municipal building collapsed in Pirganj, Rangpur.

The incident occurred while construction work was ongoing at the site, causing the structure to give way and trap several workers underneath.

Rescue operations were launched immediately to recover the victims from the debris, with local authorities and emergency services arriving at the scene.

The four injured workers were rushed to the nearest hospital for medical treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were recovered from the rubble.

Local residents and officials gathered at the site as heavy machinery was used to clear the collapsed roof and search for any other trapped individuals.

headline_marked: Govt schools: [[Lottery for Class 1, exams for Classes 2-9]]
headline: Govt schools: Lottery for Class 1, exams for Classes 2-9
summary: The education ministry has detailed the admission policy for the next academic year, bringing back entrance tests for students transferring into higher classes.
details: The education ministry has published the admission policy for government primary and secondary schools for the next academic year, covering Classes 1 to 9.
Lottery-based admission will remain the standard for Class 1. However, students seeking to transfer into Classes 2 through 9 must now sit for entrance examinations to fill vacant seats.
For Classes 2-5, the exam will be a one-hour test totaling 50 marks, covering Bangla (15), English (15), and Mathematics (20).
Students applying for Classes 6-9 will face a two-hour exam totaling 100 marks, with Bangla (30), English (30), and Mathematics (40).
Admissions to Class 1 will follow the National Education Policy 2010, requiring children to be between 5 and 7 years old as of January 1 of the academic year.
A certified copy of the online birth registration certificate is mandatory for age verification. Children with special needs may receive an age concession of up to 5 years.
caption:
Lottery for the little ones, exams for the rest. Government schools change their admission rules for Classes 2-9.

The education ministry has published the admission policy for government primary and secondary schools for the next academic year, covering Classes 1 to 9.

Lottery-based admission will remain the standard for Class 1. However, students seeking to transfer into Classes 2 through 9 must now sit for entrance examinations to fill vacant seats.

For Classes 2-5, the exam will be a one-hour test totaling 50 marks, covering Bangla (15), English (15), and Mathematics (20).

Students applying for Classes 6-9 will face a two-hour exam totaling 100 marks, with Bangla (30), English (30), and Mathematics (40).

Admissions to Class 1 will follow the National Education Policy 2010, requiring children to be between 5 and 7 years old as of January 1 of the academic year.

A certified copy of the online birth registration certificate is mandatory for age verification. Children with special needs may receive an age concession of up to 5 years.
